summary: Trulshik Rinpoche (1924–2011) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dudjom Rinpoche, A Dön Khenchen Trinlé Wanggyal, and Min Ling Khenchen Ngawang Khyentsé Norbu, and taught the 14th Dalai Lama.

Trulshik Rinpoche Ngawang Chökyi Lodrö (1923–2011) was active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He founded Thubten Chöling, served as official head of Nyingma in 2010, and taught the 14th Dalai Lama and Sogyal Rinpoche.

Truman Michelson (1879–1938) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Harvard, Leipzig, Bonn, and Columbia under Franz Boas. He worked at the Smithsonian Institution (~1910–1938), the Bureau of American Ethnology (from 1910), and George Washington University (1917–1932).
Trung Huynh is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of the West under doctoral supervisor Darui Long (attested 2016).

Trungram Gyaltrul Rinpoche (born 1968) specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute and earned a PhD from Harvard (~1997–2004) under Leonard van der Kuijp, Thomas Burke, and Khenchen Trinley Paljor Rinpoche.

Trungram Gyalwa Rinpoche (born 1968) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Harvard (PhD -2004). He held visiting positions at the University of Michigan and McGill University (2016).

Tryambak Shankar Shejwalkar (1895–1963) was an Indian historian and Indologist. He studied at the University of Mumbai and served on the faculty at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute from around 1939 to 1955.

Tryambakarama Sastri worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Lakshmana Sastri Dravida at Government Sanskrit College, Varanasi, and served as headmaster (pradhanadhyapak) at Government Sanskrit Pathashala, Jamnagar (attested 1932).
Tré Khen Zur Lozang Wangchuk was a scholar who studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, the 14th Dalai Lama, and Trijang Rinpoche.

Trịnh Xuân Thuận (born 1948) is a scholar in religious studies and other fields. He studied at the California Institute of Technology (~1967–1970), Princeton (~1970–1974), and the University of Virginia, where he held an appointment around 1979.

Tse-fu Kuan is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a doctoral thesis at the University of Oxford (-2004) under Richard Gombrich. He later conducted postdoctoral research at National Cheng Kung University and held a post at Yuan Ze University.

Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche (1914–1983) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Ganden Monastery, held a post at Ganden Jangtse Monastery, and taught the 14th Dalai Lama, Alexander Berzin, Joseph Loizzo, and Thubten Chodron.

Tsering Dhundup Gonkatsang (born 1951) works in Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Panjab University, Tibetan Children's Village, and the University of Glasgow, later serving as headmaster at Tibetan Children's Village and Tibetan instructor at Oxford (2001).
Tsering Gyaltsen is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and was a student of the traditional teacher Dudjom Rinpoche.

Tsering Shakya (born 1959) is a Tibetologist and historian who earned his BA, MPhil, and PhD from SOAS. He was a research fellow at SOAS (1999–2002), taught at Oxford, and held a Canada Research Chair at UBC (~2005).

Tsewang Gyurme is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He served as President of the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences and as president of the Tibetan Association for Sacred Studies (attested 2006).

Tsikey Chokling Rinpoche (1953–2020) was active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Young Lamas Home School and served as master of Vajrayana ceremonies at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling from around 1976 to 2020.

Tsoknyi Rinpoche (born 1966) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Khampagar Monastery (~1979–1990) under Khamtrul Rinpoche Dongyud Nyima, Dilgo Khyentse, Tulku Urgyen, Adeu Rinpoche, and Nyoshul Khenpo, and held a post at Tergar Osel Ling.

Tsu-lin Mei (1933–2023) was a scholar of linguistics and sinology. He studied at Oberlin College, Harvard, and Yale, and subsequently held academic posts at Harvard University (~1964–1971) and Cornell University (~1971–2004).

Tsuguhito Takeuchi (1951–2021) was a linguist and Tibetologist. He studied at Kyoto, Penn, and Indiana (PhD ~1980–1994) under Christopher Beckwith, Tatsuo Nishida, and others, and was Professor of Linguistics at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies (~1999–2017).
